clinicalPearls: The most common single-gene cause of Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease worldwide.
Autosomal recessive loss of the IL-12 receptor beta-1 chain, which is shared by the receptors for both IL-12 and IL-23.
Loss of IL-12 and IL-23 responsiveness impairs interferon-gamma production and Th17/IL-17 immunity together.

Typical presentations are BCG disease, environmental non-tuberculous mycobacterial infection and recurrent non-typhoidal salmonellosis; mucocutaneous candidiasis may accompany because of the IL-23/IL-17 defect.
The course is generally milder than complete interferon-gamma receptor deficiency, with incomplete clinical penetrance so that some genetically affected relatives remain healthy.
Recombinant interferon-gamma is effective because the downstream interferon-gamma receptor and STAT1 signalling remain intact.
Salmonella infection, including recurrent bacteraemia, is disproportionately common in this defect.
reference.pathophysiology: IL12RB1 encodes the beta-1 chain that pairs with IL-12 receptor beta-2 to form the IL-12 receptor and with IL-23R to form the IL-23 receptor on T and natural killer cells. Autosomal recessive loss-of-function mutations abolish surface expression of a functional receptor, so cells cannot respond to either IL-12 or IL-23. Because IL-12 is the principal signal driving interferon-gamma secretion, its loss blunts the interferon-gamma-macrophage activation axis and impairs control of intracellular mycobacteria and Salmonella; concurrent loss of IL-23 signalling impairs maintenance of interleukin-17-producing (Th17) cells, explaining the mucocutaneous candidiasis seen in some patients. Because the interferon-gamma receptor and its STAT1 signalling are intact, exogenous interferon-gamma can bypass the block, and clinical penetrance is incomplete.
additionalDifferentials: Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis from other causes such as STAT1 gain-of-function or IL-17 pathway defects
additionalInvestigations: Flow cytometry for IL-12 receptor beta-1 surface expression on activated T and natural killer cells
Whole-blood interferon-gamma production after stimulation with IL-12 (absent response) and BCG
Mycobacterial and Salmonella cultures with species identification
Assessment of Th17/IL-17 responses when candidiasis is present
Broader inborn-errors-of-immunity gene panel to exclude phenocopies
redFlags: Environmental non-tuberculous mycobacterial disease in a child
Mucocutaneous candidiasis combined with mycobacterial or salmonella disease
Family history of childhood mycobacterial or salmonella infection, especially with consanguinity
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is comparatively favourable among MSMD genotypes: many patients respond to antimicrobials and recombinant interferon-gamma and some genetically affected individuals remain asymptomatic, although disseminated disease can still be life-threatening.
pitfalls: Expecting full penetrance, since asymptomatic mutation carriers exist and a negative family history does not exclude the diagnosis.
Overlooking candidiasis as a clue to the shared IL-23/IL-17 defect.
Treating recurrent Salmonella bacteraemia as simple reinfection without an immunological work-up.
Misidentifying BCG disease as tuberculosis without typing.
Stopping antimicrobials prematurely given the tendency to relapse.
references: International Union of Immunological Societies (IUIS) inborn errors of immunity classification
management: Treat mycobacterial and non-typhoidal Salmonella infections with prolonged targeted antimicrobial regimens guided by culture and susceptibility
Use recombinant interferon-gamma as adjunctive therapy, effective because the downstream interferon-gamma receptor and STAT1 signalling remain intact
Treat mucocutaneous candidiasis with antifungal agents, reflecting the associated interleukin-23 and interleukin-17 defect
Provide antimicrobial prophylaxis for recurrent infection and strictly avoid live BCG and other live vaccines
Manage disseminated or febrile deterioration promptly with cultures and directed antimicrobials
Monitor with serial mycobacterial and Salmonella cultures and clinical surveillance for relapse
Offer genetic counselling and cascade family screening, noting the incomplete penetrance of this recessive disorder
